issues.description: Payment card details (cardNumber, CVV) are stored in plain text in the PaymentDetails interface and passed through the system unencrypted. This violates PCI DSS compliance requirements and exposes sensitive financial data. If logged, transmitted over non-HTTPS, or stored anywhere, this creates a critical data breach risk.
issues.suggestion: Never handle raw card details in your application. Use a PCI-compliant payment processor (Stripe, PayPal) that provides tokenization. Accept only payment tokens, not raw card data. If you must handle cards, achieve PCI DSS Level 1 compliance and encrypt all card data at rest and in transit using strong encryption (AES-256).

issues.description: The chargeCard function logs the full payment object to console on error (line 127), which includes the unencrypted cardNumber, CVV, and expiryDate. This exposes sensitive payment card information in application logs, violating PCI DSS and creating a critical security vulnerability.
issues.suggestion: Remove sensitive data from error logging. Use sanitized logging: console.error('Payment failed:', { lastFour: payment.cardNumber.slice(-4), amount, error: error.message }). Never log full card numbers, CVV, or other PCI data.

issues.description: Card validation is performed client-side only with basic length and format checks. There is no Luhn algorithm check for card number validity, no real-time fraud detection, and no verification with the card issuer. An attacker could submit fake card numbers that pass these weak validations.
issues.suggestion: Use a PCI-compliant payment gateway (Stripe, Braintree) that handles card validation and fraud detection. If implementing validation, add Luhn algorithm check and integrate with payment processor's card verification API. Example: use Stripe.js to tokenize cards before they reach your server.

issues.description: The expiry date validation has a critical Y2K-style bug. It assumes all years are in the 2000s by using '2000 + parseInt(year)'. When the input is '26', it becomes 2026, but in 2100, '00' would incorrectly become 2000 instead of 2100. Additionally, cards expiring in the current month may be incorrectly marked as expired due to day-of-month comparison.
issues.suggestion: Fix the date parsing logic to handle century rollover and compare year/month only: const [month, year] = expiryDate.split('/').map(Number); const currentDate = new Date(); const currentYear = currentDate.getFullYear() % 100; const currentMonth = currentDate.getMonth() + 1; const cardYear = year < 70 ? 2000 + year : 1900 + year; if (cardYear < currentDate.getFullYear() || (cardYear === currentDate.getFullYear() && month < currentMonth)) return false;

issues.description: The hasFeatureAccess function returns the raw database query result without checking if db.query returns an array. If db.query returns null or throws an error, the function will crash. Additionally, subscription.features might not be valid JSON, causing JSON.parse to throw an unhandled exception.
issues.suggestion: Add proper error handling and null checks: const result = await db.query(query, [userId]); if (!result || result.length === 0) return false; try { const features = JSON.parse(subscription.features); return Array.isArray(features) && features.includes(feature); } catch (error) { console.error('Invalid subscription data:', error); return false; }

issues.description: The getUserSubscription function assumes JSON.parse will succeed and doesn't validate the parsed data. If the database contains corrupted JSON in the features column, this function will throw an unhandled exception and crash the request.
issues.suggestion: Add try-catch around JSON parsing and validate the result: try { const features = JSON.parse(row.features); if (!Array.isArray(features)) throw new Error('Invalid features format'); return { userId: row.user_id, tier: row.tier, validUntil: new Date(row.valid_until), features }; } catch (error) { console.error('Failed to parse subscription:', error); return null; }

issues.description: The chargeCard function returns false on failure, but processPremiumPayment only returns false without rolling back or logging the failed payment attempt. If payment fails after validation, the user sees a generic failure but there's no audit trail, no retry mechanism, and no customer notification.
issues.suggestion: Implement proper error handling with audit logging: if (!paymentSuccessful) { await logFailedPayment(userId, tier, 'charge_failed'); throw new Error('Payment processing failed. Please try again or contact support.'); }. Consider implementing idempotency keys to prevent duplicate charges on retry.

issues.description: The upgradeUserSubscription function uses INSERT...ON CONFLICT which could allow subscription tier downgrades without proper authorization checks. An attacker who can call this function could potentially downgrade other users' subscriptions or manipulate subscription validity periods.
issues.suggestion: Add authorization checks before allowing subscription modifications. Implement separate functions for upgrades vs downgrades with proper access control. Add audit logging: const currentSub = await getUserSubscription(userId); if (currentSub && isDowngrade(currentSub.tier, tier)) { await requireAdminAccess(); } await auditLog('subscription_change', { userId, from: currentSub?.tier, to: tier });

issues.description: The calculateSubscriptionPrice function has hardcoded tax rate (8%) and processing fee (2.9%) that likely vary by jurisdiction and payment processor. These values should be configurable as they change based on user location and business agreements.
issues.suggestion: Move pricing configuration to a centralized config file or database: interface PricingConfig { taxRate: number; processingFee: number; basePrice: number; } async function calculateSubscriptionPrice(tier: string, userRegion: string): Promise<number> { const config = await getPricingConfig(tier, userRegion); return config.basePrice * (1 + config.taxRate + config.processingFee); }

issues.description: The hasFeatureAccess function compares dates using '<' operator which only checks if the subscription has expired, but doesn't account for timezone differences. A subscription expiring at midnight UTC might incorrectly deny access to users in different timezones on the expiry date.
issues.suggestion: Use timezone-aware date comparison or normalize to UTC: const validUntil = new Date(subscription.valid_until); const now = new Date(); validUntil.setHours(23, 59, 59, 999); // End of day in user's timezone or use a library like date-fns: if (isBefore(validUntil, startOfDay(now))) return false;

issues.description: The processPremiumPayment function validates that payment.amount >= required amount, but there's no handling for overpayment. If a user accidentally sends $100 for a $9.99 subscription, the full amount gets charged without confirmation or refund logic.
issues.suggestion: Add exact amount validation or overpayment handling: const expectedAmount = calculateSubscriptionPrice(tier); if (Math.abs(payment.amount - expectedAmount) > 0.01) { throw new Error(`Payment amount mismatch. Expected: $${expectedAmount.toFixed(2)}, Received: $${payment.amount.toFixed(2)}`); }

issues.description: The chargeCard function catches all errors and returns false, swallowing the actual error details. This makes debugging payment failures extremely difficult and prevents proper error reporting to payment monitoring systems.
issues.suggestion: Rethrow errors with context instead of silently failing: catch (error) { console.error('Payment processing error:', { lastFour, amount, error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error' }); throw new Error(`Payment processing failed: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error'}`); }

issues.description: The upgradeUserSubscription function doesn't handle database errors. If the query fails (network issue, constraint violation, etc.), the function will throw an unhandled error and the user will be charged but not upgraded.
issues.suggestion: Wrap database operations in try-catch and implement transaction rollback: try { await db.query(query, [userId, tier, validUntil, JSON.stringify(features)]); } catch (error) { console.error('Subscription upgrade failed:', { userId, tier, error }); throw new Error('Failed to activate subscription. Payment will be refunded.'); // Trigger refund workflow }

issues.description: The cardNumber validation only checks for exactly 16 digits, which excludes valid American Express cards (15 digits) and some other card types. This unnecessarily restricts payment options and may lose legitimate customers.
issues.suggestion: Support all major card types: const validLengths = [13, 14, 15, 16, 19]; // Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Diners, etc. if (!validLengths.includes(cardNumber.length) || !/^\d+$/.test(cardNumber)) return false;

issues.description: The PRICING object is defined inside the calculateSubscriptionPrice function, which means it's recreated on every call. For a heavily-used pricing function, this is inefficient and makes price updates require code changes and redeployment.
issues.suggestion: Move pricing to a module-level constant or configuration file: const SUBSCRIPTION_PRICING = { premium: 9.99, enterprise: 49.99, TAX_RATE: 0.08, PROCESSING_FEE: 0.029 } as const; Then reference it in the function. Consider loading from environment variables or a database for easier price updates.

issues.description: The processPremiumPayment function has multiple responsibilities: validation, pricing calculation, payment processing, and subscription upgrade. This violates the Single Responsibility Principle and makes the function difficult to test and maintain.
issues.suggestion: Refactor into smaller, focused functions: async function processPremiumPayment(userId: string, payment: PaymentDetails, tier: 'premium' | 'enterprise'): Promise<PaymentResult> { const validator = new PaymentValidator(); const processor = new PaymentProcessor(); const subscriptionService = new SubscriptionService(); validator.validate(payment); const charge = await processor.charge(payment, tier); await subscriptionService.upgrade(userId, tier); return charge; }

codeQuality.summary: This file contains critical PCI DSS violations by handling raw payment card data (cardNumber, CVV) in plain text and logging sensitive information. Multiple high-severity bugs exist in date validation, error handling, and data parsing that could cause payment failures or security breaches. The code lacks proper authorization checks, transaction management, and audit logging for financial operations. Immediate remediation required before production use.

testCoverage.summary: No tests exist for src/premium.ts. This file contains critical payment processing, subscription management, and feature access control logic that is completely untested. All 6 exported and internal functions lack test coverage, including security-sensitive payment validation, pricing calculations, and database operations with financial implications.

suggestions.description: Extract expiry date validation into a separate function. Currently, expiry validation logic (regex, parsing, and comparison) is embedded in a longer validation function, making it harder to test and reuse.
suggestions.benefits: Improves testability by isolating expiry validation logic, reduces cyclomatic complexity of the parent function, and enables reuse of expiry validation elsewhere.

suggestions.description: Replace multiple early-return conditionals with a single compound boolean expression. The function currently has 4 separate if-return blocks that can be combined for better readability.
suggestions.benefits: Reduces function complexity from multiple exit points to one, makes validation rules immediately visible, and creates self-documenting variable names that explain what each check validates.

suggestions.description: Extract pricing configuration and calculation into a PricingStrategy pattern. Currently pricing logic mixes configuration (rates, fees) with calculation, making it hard to test different pricing models or adjust rates.
suggestions.benefits: Enables dependency injection for testing with different rates, separates configuration from logic, allows easy price adjustments without code changes, and makes pricing rules explicit and centralized.

suggestions.description: Extract feature set configuration into a constant map and extract the subscription validity calculation. The ternary operator with hard-coded feature arrays is difficult to maintain as tiers grow.
suggestions.benefits: Centralizes feature configuration for easier maintenance, makes adding new tiers simpler, improves testability of date calculation, and eliminates hard-coded duplication between tiers.

suggestions.description: Introduce early returns for clarity and reduce nesting. The current structure checks subscription existence, validity, and feature inclusion in a nested manner.
suggestions.benefits: Reduces indentation levels, makes the validation flow clearer with guard clauses, adds type safety to JSON.parse, and improves readability by introducing a descriptive isExpired variable.

suggestions.description: Extract common subscription fetching logic into a reusable function. Both functions query the database identically and handle empty results, violating DRY principle.
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates duplication, centralizes database query logic for easier modification, reduces the chance of inconsistent subscription fetching, and simplifies both calling functions.

suggestions.description: Use destructuring and object shorthand when mapping database row to Subscription object. The current approach manually accesses each property.
suggestions.benefits: Reduces repetition of 'row.' accessor, makes it clear which fields are being used, adds type safety to JSON.parse, and follows modern JavaScript destructuring patterns.

suggestions.description: Extract last-four extraction and improve error handling by returning meaningful error information instead of just boolean. The current implementation loses error context.
suggestions.benefits: Extracts reusable card masking logic, propagates errors to caller instead of silently returning false (enabling better error handling in processPremiumPayment), and provides more context in error messages.

refactorings.summary: The file has several high-impact refactoring opportunities focused on extracting configuration from logic, reducing code duplication, and improving testability. Key improvements include introducing a pricing strategy pattern, centralizing feature configuration, extracting common database query logic, and simplifying validation functions with better structure and early returns.

recommendations.description: Replace direct credit card handling with PCI-compliant payment processor. Use Stripe, PayPal, or similar service that provides tokenization. Never store or log raw card numbers, CVV, or expiry dates in your application code or logs.
Remove sensitive payment data from error logging immediately. The chargeCard function logs the full payment object including cardNumber and CVV on line 127, creating a critical PCI DSS violation.

Create comprehensive test suite for payment processing functions. Start with processPremiumPayment, validatePaymentDetails, calculateSubscriptionPrice, and chargeCard - these handle financial transactions and have 0% test coverage.
Add integration tests for subscription upgrade workflow including payment failure scenarios, database rollback, and error handling paths to prevent charging users without granting subscriptions.

Implement proper card validation using Luhn algorithm and integrate with payment processor's card verification API. Current validation only checks length and format, allowing fake card numbers through.

Fix Y2K-style bug in expiry date validation (line 90). The code assumes all years are in 2000s and will fail in 2100. Also fix month-level comparison to prevent incorrectly rejecting cards expiring in current month.
Add error handling and JSON validation to hasFeatureAccess and getUserSubscription functions. Wrap JSON.parse in try-catch and validate array types to prevent crashes from corrupted database data.
Implement audit logging for all payment and subscription operations. Track failed payments, subscription changes, and authorization attempts for compliance, debugging, and fraud detection.
Add edge case tests for payment validation including expired cards, invalid CVV lengths, malformed expiry dates, insufficient payment amounts, and AMEX cards (15 digits, 4-digit CVV).
Extract pricing configuration into a centralized PricingStrategy pattern with dependency injection support. This enables testing with different rates and allows price changes without code deployment.

Add authorization checks to upgradeUserSubscription to prevent unauthorized subscription modifications or downgrades. Implement separate functions for upgrades vs downgrades with proper access control.
Move hardcoded tax rates and processing fees to configuration. These values vary by jurisdiction and payment processor - make them configurable based on user region and business agreements.

Implement transaction management and rollback for payment processing. If subscription upgrade fails after charging, automatically trigger refund workflow to prevent charging users without granting access.
Extract common database query logic for subscription fetching into a reusable helper function to eliminate duplication between hasFeatureAccess and getUserSubscription.
